title: Combo preview script keys bones that armature_add never creates
body:
## Summary
comboAnimationScript adds a default armature (one bone named "Bone") and then keys pose.bones["Spine"] and ["UpperArm.R"], which do not exist, so every combo with at least one hit raises KeyError.

## Description
src/lib/blender-mcp/scripts/combo-animation.ts:33 runs bpy.ops.object.armature_add, which creates a single bone named "Bone". Lines 22-25 then index armature.pose.bones["Spine"] and ["UpperArm.R"] for every hit. Neither bone is created anywhere in the script. The only caller, src/components/modules/content/animations/AIComboChoreographer/useAIComboChoreographer.ts:80, therefore gets an addon error for every combo it sends. Fixed means the script creates the bones it keys (in edit mode, before entering pose mode) or keys only bones it created, and ends with a receipt.

## Flow
- Combo choreographer: generate a combo with >= 1 hit, press Send to Blender
- comboAnimationScript -> /api/blender-mcp/execute -> addon runs armature_add, then pose.bones["Spine"]
- KeyError: bpy_prop_collection[key]: key "Spine" not found; the UI shows the error and nothing is keyed

## Expected impact
The combo-to-Blender preview starts working at all. Risk: the bone layout chosen for the preview is a design call. The fix only has to make the keyed names exist.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - the combo preview runs instead of raising on its first hit
Before: by reading the code: 1 of 1 hit-bearing combos raises KeyError (armature_add yields bone "Bone" only; the script reads "Spine", "UpperArm.R")
After: predicted 0 of 1 once the script creates Spine/UpperArm.R before pose mode
Method: simulation - Blender is not run in gates, so no headless Blender arm was available this round
Result: better
Gate: none
impact: The combo-to-Blender preview starts working at all. Risk: the bone layout chosen for the preview is a design call. The fix only has to make the keyed names exist.
instrument: headless Blender 4.2 run of comboAnimationScript with one hit (operator machine), or a contract test that every pose.bones["X"] the script reads is created by the script

title: SCRIPT_CATALOG is hand-maintained and misses 5 receipted emitters
body:
## Summary
The receipt contract test sweeps SCRIPT_CATALOG, a hand-kept list of 10 emitters. Five emitters that do print receipts are not on it, and seven prose-only emitters are not listed anywhere.

## Description
src/lib/blender-mcp/scripts/catalog.ts:34 lists 10 emitters, and src/__tests__/lib/blender-mcp/script-contract.test.ts:90 only checks `length >= 10`. Missing receipted emitters: create-armature (kind "armature"), export-scene ("export"), generate-lods ("lod"), mesh-stats ("mesh-stats"), composition-blockout ("blockout"). Some have their own tests, but none is under the shared "last statement is a receipt" contract. Prose-only emitters: combo-animation, create-material, dungeon-to-geometry, uv-projection, dissolve/fire/water, scene-objects (x2). The catalog doc says a new emitter "belongs here", but nothing enforces that. This is the hand-maintained-list class (SKILL 4.7): the test reads the implementation's own list.

## Flow
- Enumerate exported *Script functions from the scripts directory (ground truth)
- Diff against SCRIPT_CATALOG ids + an explicit prose-only list with reasons
- Add the 5 missing receipted entries, with values for their receipt expressions

## Expected impact
A new emitter can no longer skip the receipt contract silently. Test-only change, so it cannot break runtime.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - receipt-contract coverage derived from the tree, not a list
Before: 10 of 15 receipted emitters under the contract; 0 of 9 prose-only emitters declared
After: 15 of 15 under the contract; 9 of 9 declared with reasons
Method: probe - grep of pyReceipt across scripts/ against catalog.ts ids; not built this round (M, and part of the list is a design call)
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
grep pyReceipt src/lib/blender-mcp/scripts -> create-armature.ts:41, export-scene.ts:60, generate-lods.ts:65, mesh-stats.ts:40, composition-blockout.ts:82 not in catalog.ts:34-115
script-contract.test.ts:92 expect(SCRIPT_CATALOG.length).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(10)
impact: A new emitter can no longer skip the receipt contract silently. Test-only change, so it cannot break runtime.
instrument: a contract test that lists src/lib/blender-mcp/scripts/**/*.ts and requires every exported *Script emitter to appear in SCRIPT_CATALOG or in a prose-only allow-list that gives a reason

title: Four script emitters have zero production callers
body:
## Summary
applyTextureScript, autoWeightsScript, setupIKScript and worldAlignedUvScript have no caller outside src/lib/blender-mcp and its tests. apply-texture also wires AO to a Principled BSDF socket that does not exist.

## Description
A grep of src/ (excluding __tests__ and src/lib/blender-mcp/) finds 0 consumers for each of the four. Three of them stay "tested" only because SCRIPT_CATALOG lists them. src/lib/blender-mcp/scripts/apply-texture.ts:14 maps the ao slot to bsdf.inputs["Ambient Occlusion"]. Principled BSDF has no such input, as src/lib/blender-mcp/scripts/create-material.ts:86 itself states, so the ao slot raises KeyError. The context-map description names IK setup and UV projection as capabilities, so deleting them is a direction call, not a sweep fix. The two options are to wire them to a surface, or to remove them along with their catalog rows.

## Flow
- grep -rlw <emitter> src | grep -v __tests__ | grep -v src/lib/blender-mcp/ -> 0 for each
- Operator decides keep (wire a caller, fix the AO slot like create-material does) or delete

## Expected impact
About 160 LOC either carries a caller or goes away. Deleting them would also drop 3 catalog rows.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - no shipped-but-unreachable emitters
Before: 4 emitters, 0 production consumers each; apply-texture ao slot targets a nonexistent socket
After: 0 unreachable emitters
Method: probe - zero-consumer grep run this round; removal not built because the context scope names these capabilities
Result: better
Gate: direction
evidence:
zero-consumer grep: applyTextureScript 0, autoWeightsScript 0, setupIKScript 0, worldAlignedUvScript 0 (src/, excl. __tests__ and src/lib/blender-mcp/)
src/lib/blender-mcp/scripts/apply-texture.ts:14 ao: 'Ambient Occlusion'
src/lib/blender-mcp/scripts/create-material.ts:86 "there is no AO input on the BSDF"
impact: About 160 LOC either carries a caller or goes away. Deleting them would also drop 3 catalog rows.
instrument: n/a - the decision is whether the capabilities the context description names (IK setup, UV projection) are kept

title: Generation wire vocabulary unverified against the ahujasid addon
body:
## Summary
service.ts sends {prompt} / {job_id} and reads jobId/status/progress/resultUrl/objectName. From memory of addon.py, the upstream addon takes text_prompt and answers with provider-native keys (uuid, jobs.subscription_key, request_id), so a real job may never carry the jobId the app keys on.

## Description
src/lib/blender-mcp/service.ts:475 (createJob) sends params {prompt}. pollJobStatus (:553) sends {job_id}. The service reads data.jobId / data.status / data.progress / data.resultUrl. Every test fixture uses the app's own vocabulary (src/__tests__/api/blender-mcp-generate-ledger.test.ts:42 mocks {jobId:"j1"}), so nothing in the tree checks the shape against the addon. Since commit 3f5907b6 a missing jobId fails loudly instead of being ledgered as '', which makes this mismatch visible if it is real. Deciding it needs the live addon. It is a contract with a consumer outside this tree.

## Flow
- Operator: enable Hyper3D in the addon, POST /api/blender-mcp/generate
- Record the raw create reply and a poll reply
- Align createJob/pollJobStatus/importGeneratedAsset params and keys; pin fixtures

## Expected impact
Paid generations become trackable end to end. Today the honest state is "unknown". Risk: the addon's shape differs across versions and modes.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - a paid generation is tracked by the id the addon actually returns
Before: unverified: 0 fixtures taken from a real addon reply
After: fixtures recorded from the live addon; create/poll/import keyed on its real fields
Method: simulation - the addon source is external and the network/Blender are out of bounds for a round; recollection of addon.py is not evidence
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: contract
impact: Paid generations become trackable end to end. Today the honest state is "unknown". Risk: the addon's shape differs across versions and modes.
instrument: operator act: run create/poll/import against a live ahujasid blender-mcp addon (Hyper3D + Hunyuan3D modes) and record the reply shapes; then pin them in mockBlenderServer fixtures

title: pollJobStatus passes unvalidated status and NaN progress through
body:
## Summary
pollJobStatus casts whatever status string the addon sends to JobStatus and runs Number() on progress, so a provider word like "Done" never terminates the forge poll and a non-numeric progress becomes NaN.

## Description
src/lib/blender-mcp/service.ts:561-563 does `(data?.status as JobStatus) ?? 'pending'` and `Number(data?.progress ?? 0)`. The status route (src/app/api/blender-mcp/generate/status/route.ts:24) only acts on exactly "failed"/"completed", so any other terminal word keeps the job "generating" in the ledger forever (until the 24h TTL), and mcpGateForJob never grades it. Fixed means normalising into the union: a known synonym map, otherwise "processing", plus logging the unknown word; progress gets clamped to a finite 0-100. The synonym list depends on the wire card above.

## Flow
- Addon answers {status:"Done", progress:"n/a"}
- pollJobStatus returns status "Done", progress NaN
- Forge queue polls forever; the ledger keeps the job resumable

## Expected impact
A finished generation is recognised as finished. Risk: a wrong synonym map could mark an unfinished job complete.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - every polled job reports a status inside the JobStatus union
Before: by reading: 3 of 3 off-vocabulary replies leave the union or yield NaN
After: predicted 0 of 3
Method: simulation - the instrument is S but the synonym map is blocked on the wire-vocabulary card
Result: better
Gate: none
impact: A finished generation is recognised as finished. Risk: a wrong synonym map could mark an unfinished job complete.
instrument: unit test over the mock socket: replies {status:"Done"}, {status:"COMPLETED"}, {progress:"abc"} -> assert a JobStatus from the union and a finite 0-100 progress

title: Generation-ledger write failures are invisible
body:
## Summary
saveLedgerFile returns false on any write failure and its only caller ignores the return value, so a disk or permission failure silently stops paid jobs from surviving a restart.

## Description
src/lib/blender-mcp/ledger-file.ts:41-53 catches every error and returns false. src/lib/blender-mcp/generation-ledger.ts:110 calls it and drops the result, and ledgerFileWriteCount is read only by tests. Silent in-memory degradation is the documented design (ledger-file.ts header). What is missing is any signal that the degradation happened. The operator finds out only after a restart, when a paid job is gone. Fixed means one logger.warn per failure streak, naming the file and the error.

## Flow
- .pof/ becomes read-only (or the path is a directory)
- ledger.record -> coalescer -> saveLedgerFile returns false
- Nothing is logged; after restart listResumable() is empty

## Expected impact
A broken persistence path gets one log line instead of a lost paid job. Risk: none to behaviour.

## Evaluation
Claim: observability - a failed ledger write leaves a trace
Before: 0 log lines per failed write (return value unread: 1 call site)
After: 1 warn per failure streak
Method: simulation - the S instrument was not built this round (budget went to the 5 Lane A fixes)
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
src/lib/blender-mcp/ledger-file.ts:41-53 (catch -> return false)
src/lib/blender-mcp/generation-ledger.ts:110 saveLedgerFile(...) result discarded
grep saveLedgerFile src (non-test): 1 caller
impact: A broken persistence path gets one log line instead of a lost paid job. Risk: none to behaviour.
instrument: test: setLedgerFileForTest(<path under an unwritable dir or a directory path>), record a job, flush, assert one logger.warn naming the file (and no warn on success)

title: Six of ten bridge error strings diagnose as "unknown"
body:
## Summary
classifyConnectionError recognises connect-time errors, but the in-flight errors the service also produces (closed mid-command, ECONNRESET, reset while queued, oversize reply, not connected, write failed) all fall through to "Could not connect to Blender: Unexpected error".

## Description
src/lib/blender-mcp/diagnostics.ts:68-177 matches timeout, refused, DNS and "not responding". The service emits 10 distinct error shapes (service.ts:102, 115, 135, 253, 267, 315, 321, 322, 338, 397). Only 4 of them reach a named mode. The other 6 show the generic checklist in BlenderConnectionBar.tsx:117 and BlenderSetupWizard.tsx:71, even though the cause is known: for example, Blender quitting mid-command ("Connection closed while command was in flight") deserves a "Blender closed the connection" diagnosis.

## Flow
- Operator quits Blender while a script runs
- service settles "Connection closed while command was in flight"
- Connection bar: "Unexpected error: Connection closed ..." with the generic checklist

## Expected impact
Operators get a named cause for the commonest in-flight failures. Risk: copy only.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - every error the bridge itself produces gets a named diagnosis
Before: 6 of 10 service error strings classify as unknown
After: 0 of 10 (new modes or mappings for closed/reset/oversize)
Method: probe - walked each service.ts err() string through the matcher by reading; not built because the new copy is a UX decision
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
src/lib/blender-mcp/diagnostics.ts:148-233 matchers
unknown: service.ts:253 "reset while queued", :267 "Not connected", :321 "closed while in flight", :322 "Socket error: ECONNRESET", :338 "Response exceeded", :397 "Write failed"
impact: Operators get a named cause for the commonest in-flight failures. Risk: copy only.
instrument: table test: feed each err() string service.ts can produce through classifyConnectionError and assert none lands in "unknown" except a genuinely unknown one

title: Byte limits on the bridge are measured in UTF-16 code units
body:
## Summary
MAX_RESPONSE_BYTES ("8MB") is compared with buffer.length, and executeCode's "100KB limit" with code.length. Both are counts of UTF-16 units, so non-ASCII payloads can exceed the stated byte bounds by up to 3x.

## Description
src/lib/blender-mcp/service.ts:31 documents an 8 MB receive ceiling, but service.ts:340 compares buffer.length, which counts characters, not bytes. service.ts:422 refuses code.length > 100_000 with the message "Code exceeds 100KB limit". Fixed means counting chunk.length (bytes) as chunks arrive and using Buffer.byteLength(code). Impact is low: the cap exists to stop garbage floods, and ASCII is unaffected.

## Flow
- Addon streams a CJK-heavy reply
- cap trips at 8M characters = up to 24 MB

## Expected impact
The stated limits become true. Risk: negligible.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - documented byte limits enforced in bytes
Before: 2 of 2 limits measured in UTF-16 units
After: 0 of 2
Method: probe - read both comparison sites; XS but outside the round's priority after the UTF-8 decoder fix
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
src/lib/blender-mcp/service.ts:31 MAX_RESPONSE_BYTES = 8 * 1024 * 1024
src/lib/blender-mcp/service.ts:340 if (buffer.length > MAX_RESPONSE_BYTES)
src/lib/blender-mcp/service.ts:422 code.length > 100_000 -> "Code exceeds 100KB limit"
impact: The stated limits become true. Risk: negligible.
instrument: test: a reply of 3-byte characters just over 8 MB (in bytes) but under 8M code units must trip the cap; executeCode with 60k 2-byte chars (>100 KB) must be refused
